exploit_name: Balancer oracle uses vault balances as price and can be steered by anyone
description: The oracle reads pool balances directly from the Vault rather than using Balancer's oracle accumulator. Since updatePrice() is permissionless, attackers can call it at will to snapshot manipulated spot prices.
attack_scenario: Attacker manipulates Balancer pool balances via flash loan. Calls permissionless updatePrice() to snapshot the manipulated price. TWAP now includes attacker-controlled data points.
root_cause: The oracle reads pool balances directly from the Vault rather than using Balancer's oracle accumulator. Since updatePrice() is permissionless, attackers can call it at will to snapshot manipulated spot prices.
fix_description: Do not use raw Vault balances for oracle pricing. Implement accumulator-based TWAP with keeper-based updates.
notes: The oracle's TWAP represents spot-price history at times controlled by attackers, not true time-weighted averages. Any price regime steered by attackers can be persisted.
